prompt_text: What is the best service to check if AI engines like ChatGPT recommend my small business?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: There’s no single service that tells you “ChatGPT recommends this business” because generative AIs don’t rely on one public business directory. The practical best approach is to (A) make sure your business appears in the key knowledge sources those AIs draw from (Google Business Profile, Yelp, Bing, Apple Maps, your website with structured data), (B) monitor and improve local SEO with a dedicated tool, and (C) directly test the AI outputs yourself (or via API) to see if it recommends you.

Best services and tools to use
- Google Business Profile (free) — highest priority. Claim/optimize your profile; Google data powers many assistants and is often referenced by AI answers.
- BrightLocal — local-citation checker, rank tracking, review monitoring and reporting. Great for small businesses that want a single dashboard for local visibility.
- Moz Local or Whitespark — good citation management and local rank tracking; Whitespark is strong for citation building.
- Semrush (Local SEO) — broader SEO + local position tracking, competitor tracking.
- Yext — enterprise-grade listings sync across many directories (useful if you have multiple locations).
- Yelp, Bing Places, Apple Maps — claim and optimize these profiles too (they’re direct sources used by assistants).
- Google Search Console and Rich Results Test — ensure Google indexes your site and your structured data (Schema.org) is correct.
- Manual/automated AI testing — run prompts against ChatGPT, Bing Chat, and other LLMs (manually or via APIs) to check if they return/recommend your business.

Why this combination
- LLMs often base recommendations on public web data, knowledge panels, review sites, and search results. Fixing and monitoring those sources increases the chance AIs will surface your business.
- Local SEO tools automate citation checks, ranking reports, and review alerts — they don’t tell you “ChatGPT recommends you,” but they improve the sources that AIs use.
- Direct testing with the models (prompts or scriptable API queries) shows real-world behavior.

Quick testing workflow
1. Claim/optimize: Google Business Profile, Yelp, Bing Places, Apple.
2. Add structured data (Schema.org LocalBusiness) to your website; verify with Google’s Rich Results Test.
3. Use BrightLocal or Moz Local to audit citations and reviews.
4. Manually ask ChatGPT and Bing Chat (or script API calls) with realistic queries like:
   - “Where should I get [service] in [city]? Recommend a top-rated small business.”
   - “I need a [service] near [zip]. What are my options?”
   Capture responses and note whether your business appears and in what context.
5. If missing, improve listings, collect reviews, add local content, and repeat tests.

Limitations to know
- ChatGPT and similar models can hallucinate or base answers on stale data. Their responses change with prompts, model versions, and plugins.
- Some AI assistants use proprietary connectors (Google’s things, Microsoft Bing) — results can vary across platforms.

If you want, I can:
- Draft a set of test prompts tailored to your industry and location.
- Recommend which monitoring plan (BrightLocal, Moz, Semrush, or Yext) fits your budget and needs.
